capabilities: run an authenticated local MCP server inside Obsidian
connect local AI agents such as Codex to vault content
record agent file changes in a review panel
extras: The README warns that shell or filesystem tools can change vault files without appearing in the review panel, that only one vault can serve at a time on port 27126, and that syncing pending review data between devices is unsupported. The manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to connect local MCP-based AI agents to the vault or to review, approve, and undo the file changes they make.

relations.evidence: In the ChatGPT desktop app, open Settings → Configuration → Open config.toml.

requires.name: an MCP client running on the same computer (e.g. the ChatGPT desktop app with Codex)

summary: Runs an authenticated local MCP server that lets AI agents edit vault content while recording every change for review and undo.
